planted_reason: Felsenstein's pruning algorithm for phylogenetic likelihood IS sum-product on a tree: same recursion, same complexity, derived independently in 1981. Phylogenetics names it after a person, graphical models names it after the operation. Directly checkable — both compute the marginal of a product of local factors in one post-order sweep. This is the alias case, not a rediscovery: both fields name it, they just name it differently.

Ewens (1972, population genetics) and Ferguson (1973, Bayesian nonparametrics) independently derived the same exchangeable random partition. The Ewens sampling formula gives the distribution of allele-frequency classes under the infinite-alleles model; it is also the CRP partition marginal with concentration theta. Checkable: the two partition probability formulas are the same formula. The strongest of these three — a genuine parallel derivation across two fields that still barely cite each other.

A continuous-time Markov process on set partitions of {1..n} in which each pair merges at rate 1 — a probability object carrying a biological name. NOT the same as the Wright-Fisher diffusion: those two are moment-dual, forward and backward in time, and merging them would be a wrong identification. If the duality turns out to carry weight, Wright-Fisher diffusion deserves its own entry rather than an alias line here.
